title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree 3rd Point The Challenge Of Eloquence And Its Inimitability

questions.question: What did the desert poet do right after hearing one verse of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: He bowed down in prostration.

questions.question: Why did that poet say he prostrated?
questions.answer: He was moved by the amazing beauty and power of the verse’s language.

questions.question: Did he say he had become Muslim at that moment, or did he give another reason?
questions.answer: He gave another reason and said it was because of the verse’s eloquence.

questions.question: What have many experts in language and rhetoric agreed about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They agreed that its eloquence is beyond what people can produce.

questions.question: What challenge does the Qur’an give to proud writers and speakers?
questions.answer: It challenges them to bring even one chapter like it.

questions.question: What does it show that the opponents did not meet that challenge?
questions.answer: It shows they were not able to do it.

questions.question: What kinds of Arabic books are mentioned besides the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Some were written by supporters trying to imitate it, and some by enemies trying to oppose it.

questions.question: How does the passage compare those books with the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It says none of them reached the Qur’an’s level.

questions.question: What would an ordinary listener likely notice when hearing the Qur’an and other books?
questions.answer: The person would notice that the Qur’an is in a higher class and does not sound like the others.

questions.question: According to the passage, can any sensible person say the Qur’an is lower than those books?
questions.answer: No. The passage says no unbeliever or foolish person can truly say that.

questions.question: What main quality of the Qur’an is being highlighted in this passage?
questions.answer: Its unmatched eloquence and superiority in speech.

questions.question: Who is described at the beginning of the passage: a ruler, a merchant, or a Bedouin poet?
questions.answer: A Bedouin poet.

questions.question: What happened when he heard a verse recited?
questions.answer: He immediately fell into prostration.

questions.question: What question did people ask him after that?
questions.answer: They asked whether he had accepted Islam.

questions.question: How did he answer them?
questions.answer: He said no and explained that he bowed because of the verse’s powerful wording.

questions.question: What does this moment show about the effect of the Qur’an’s language?
questions.answer: It shows the Qur’an’s speech can deeply affect a person right away.

questions.question: What have thousands of scholars of rhetoric decided together?
questions.answer: They decided that the Qur’an’s eloquence cannot be matched by human beings.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention proud and self-centered writers?
questions.answer: To show that even those people were challenged to match the Qur’an and still could not.

questions.question: What was the “short way” open to the Qur’an’s opponents?
questions.answer: The short way was to produce one surah like it.

questions.question: What does their choosing a harder and riskier way prove?
questions.answer: It proves the easier challenge could not be met.

questions.question: Were only friendly writers unable to match the Qur’an, or were enemy writers unable too?
questions.answer: Both groups were unable to match it.

questions.question: What final conclusion is made about the Qur’an’s place among books?
questions.answer: It stands above all of them in eloquence.

questions.question: What kind of person heard the verse in the first example?
questions.answer: A poet from the desert.

questions.question: What was surprising about his reaction to the verse?
questions.answer: He prostrated immediately even though he did not say he had become Muslim then.

questions.question: What reason did he give for his action?
questions.answer: He was honoring the verse’s extraordinary beauty in expression.

questions.question: Why is the story of this poet important in the passage?
questions.answer: It gives an example of how strong the Qur’an’s eloquence is, even to someone hearing it briefly.

questions.question: Which group of people is said to agree that the Qur’an is beyond human ability?
questions.answer: Many scholars and experts in language and rhetoric.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an ask its challengers to produce?
questions.answer: A single surah like it.

questions.question: What warning is joined to that challenge?
questions.answer: The challengers are told that if they fail, they face disgrace and loss.

questions.question: How does the passage use the behavior of early opponents as evidence?
questions.answer: It says they did not answer the challenge directly, which shows they could not.

questions.question: What two kinds of books tried to come near the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Books from friends trying to imitate it and books from enemies trying to attack it.

questions.question: What judgment would even a common person make after listening?
questions.answer: The person would say the Qur’an is not like those books and belongs to a higher level.

questions.question: What overall claim does the passage make about human writing compared with the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Human writing cannot equal the Qur’an.

questions.question: In the first example, what caused the poet to prostrate?
questions.answer: Hearing a Qur’anic verse recited.

questions.question: What does his answer tell us about how he viewed that verse?
questions.answer: He saw it as having amazing beauty and strength in its wording.

questions.question: What is one lesson from this story about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Its language can make a strong impact even on someone outside the Muslim faith.

questions.question: What field were the named scholars experts in?
questions.answer: They were experts in eloquence and rhetoric.

questions.question: What was their united conclusion about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Its eloquence is unreachable for human beings.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an speak to arrogant writers in the passage?
questions.answer: It calls them to try making one chapter like it.

questions.question: Why does the passage say their pride would be broken by this challenge?
questions.answer: Because they thought highly of themselves but still could not answer it.

questions.question: What does the passage say happened instead of them meeting the challenge?
questions.answer: They chose dangerous opposition rather than producing a matching surah.

questions.question: What does the mention of many Arabic books help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove that, although many books exist, none rise to the Qur’an’s rank.

questions.question: According to the passage, how can a regular person tell the difference?
questions.answer: By listening, the person can tell the Qur’an is not in the same category as other books.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the fact that it is not lower than the other books?
questions.answer: Its eloquence must be above them all.

questions.question: What immediate action did the Bedouin poet take after hearing a verse?
questions.answer: He made prostration at once.

questions.question: When people asked if he had entered Islam, what did he make clear?
questions.answer: He made clear that his prostration was for the verse’s eloquence, not a claim that he had just become Muslim.

questions.question: What does this event suggest about the power of the Qur’an’s words?
questions.answer: It suggests they can move a listener very deeply.

questions.question: What have many language scholars said about anyone trying to equal the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They said it is beyond human power to equal it.

questions.question: What exact kind of response does the Qur’an ask for from its challengers?
questions.answer: It asks them to produce one surah like it.

questions.question: Why is failing to produce even one surah important evidence?
questions.answer: Because it shows the challenge was too great for them to meet.

questions.question: What are the two motives mentioned for writing other Arabic books?
questions.answer: Some were written to copy the Qur’an, and others to oppose and criticize it.

questions.question: What result did all those efforts share?
questions.answer: None of them reached the Qur’an’s level.

questions.question: How does the passage use the viewpoint of an ordinary listener?
questions.answer: It says even an average person can hear that the Qur’an is unlike the others.

questions.question: If the Qur’an is not below the other books, what must be true?
questions.answer: It must be above them.

questions.question: Which big idea ties the whole passage together?
questions.answer: The Qur’an’s speech is unique and unmatched.

questions.question: What kind of example opens this passage: a battle story, a trade story, or a listening story?
questions.answer: A listening story.

questions.question: Who is the listener in that story?
questions.answer: A Bedouin poet.

questions.question: What was his response to hearing the recited verse?
questions.answer: He immediately prostrated.

questions.question: How did he explain that response?
questions.answer: He said he was honoring the verse’s eloquence.

questions.question: After this example, what larger claim is made by many scholars?
questions.answer: That the Qur’an’s eloquence is beyond human ability.

questions.question: What challenge has the Qur’an given from early times onward?
questions.answer: It has challenged people to bring a single surah like it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the people who were too stubborn to accept the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They did not meet the challenge and chose another path instead.

questions.question: Why does that choice count as proof against them?
questions.answer: Because if they could have matched the Qur’an, they would have taken that easier way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the many Arabic books written through the years?
questions.answer: Whether written by supporters or enemies, none equaled the Qur’an.

questions.question: What simple test is mentioned for noticing the difference?
questions.answer: Listening to the Qur’an and the other books shows they are not on the same level.

questions.question: What final judgment does the passage make about the Qur’an’s eloquence?
questions.answer: It is higher than all other books.
